title: New insulin after diabetic ketoacidosis, Spanish
source:
DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS - Endocrinology
Patient: Ana Torres   MRN: 99018234   DOB: 05/02/1998
Attending: Dr. James Okafor

Diagnosis: Diabetic ketoacidosis, new diagnosis of type 1 diabetes.

MEDICATIONS
NEW: Insulin glargine 18 units under the skin once daily at 9 PM.
NEW: Insulin lispro under the skin with each meal: 1 unit for every 10 g of carbohydrate, plus correction scale per handout.
STOP: Metformin 500 mg - type 1 diabetes does not respond to metformin.

Check blood glucose before each meal and at bedtime. Record all values.
Hypoglycemia: if glucose below 70 mg/dL, take 15 g of fast sugar (4 glucose tablets or 1/2 cup juice) and recheck in 15 minutes.
Never skip insulin glargine, even if you are not eating. Call the diabetes team if you are sick and cannot eat.
Return precautions: Go to the Emergency Department for vomiting that will not stop, glucose above 300 mg/dL twice in a row with ketones, confusion, or trouble breathing.

Follow-up: Diabetes education class on 10/20/2026. Endocrinology clinic with Dr. Okafor on 10/28/2026.
